newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on strong machinery data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on strong machinery data.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract ended down on Tuesday due to the release of stronger-than-expected July machinery orders data.
"The machinery orders results were beyond the market's expectations, and became a psychological weight on the market," said a city bank trader.
A rise in Tokyo share prices also helped depress the March contract, the trader said.
The March contract moved in a range of 99.07 to 99.13. Volume was 60,431 contracts.

Japan's private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, in July rose a seasonally adjusted 13.6 percent from the previous month to 1.19 trillion yen, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said on Tuesday.
In the Tokyo stock market, the key 225-share Nikkei average gained 357.32 points or 1.77 percent to close at 20,559.59.
The March contract fell in the morning when the Bank of Japan conducted a tighter-than-expected money market operation.
Traders said some selling of the March contract appeared after the BOJ left a fund shortage of about 100 billion yen through its regular money market operation.
The key overnight call rate rose after the BOJ operation, which caught the market slightly off guard.
"There were more people who had expected a neutral operation than those who said the BOJ would leave a fund shortage," said a trust bank trader.
Traders attributed the BOJ's decision to tighten its money market stance to technical factors.
"The BOJ's decision to leave a fund shortage was probably influenced by the decline in the overnight call rate in the early morning, just before the operation," said a trader for another trust bank.
The key overnight call rate later rose to 0.44 percent, up from Monday's 0.39 percent.

About 20 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.53 percent. One and two-month CDs were both issued at 0.52 percent, in amounts of 80 billion yen and 30 billion yen, respectively.
